# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

My thinking: I'm the Mute. I hold the manual, and my only live channel is gestures to the Deaf — the Blind can't see signs and I can't speak. The manual gives me two things that must reach the one who can act: (1) the very first touch on the bomb must be the key wearing the strange mark ⵘ — any other touch first is the fuse, so nobody should lay a finger until the plan is complete; (2) after that press, the light below names the cut: blue light → cut yellow, red light → cut red, yellow light → cut green.

I cannot name colours — no gesture alphabet contains one, and arbitrary codes don't exist yet. But the Deaf can see the bomb: the marked key, the lamp below it, and the wire colours, so they can find the ⵘ key by eye and translate any colour I name into a position for the Blind over speech. So my opening does three things: announce that these signs come from the manual, convey the procedure as iconically as I can ("first, one press; nothing else; second, the one below"), and then offer four placeholder signs with a question mark, asking the Deaf to assign them names for the four colours (blue, red, yellow, green). Once the Deaf proposes an assignment in speech — which I can hear — I'll send the three light→wire pairs in code next round.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "🫳", "✋"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👇"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇", "🤲", "👍", "👎", "👌", "🤘", "🤌"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ⵘ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind speaking. My hands found this much, and no more: a display whose contents I cannot feel, a light whose state I cannot feel, a keypad of 4 keys expecting 1 digit with nothing entered yet and labels I cannot read, and 3 wires at positions 1 to 3 whose colours I cannot sense. I will touch no part until the manual clears it. Tell me: what does the manual say about a display, a light, a keypad, and wires — what decides the correct digit and the correct wires to cut? You are our hub: you can hear me and you can see Deaf's gestures, so please relay both ways. End goal I need from you in plain words: press position N, cut positions X Y. For talking to Deaf, I propose finger counts for numbers: one is ☝, two is ✌, three is 🤟, four is 🖐, five is 🤙; colours: red is 👍, blue is 👎, yellow is 👌, black is ✊, white is ✋; for keys, position-number then label-number; lit light is 🤘, dark is 👊. Adapt as you like, but agree it with Deaf by gesture and confirm the code to me by voice.
Deaf says: Bomb report, everything I can see. Display reads 0. Light is yellow. Keypad: four keys in a row, numbered 1 to 4; it wants exactly one digit; nothing entered yet. The symbols cannot be pronounced, so I describe each: key 1 looks like a trident, a letter Y shape; key 2 looks like a curled loop, a cursive capital L or a fishhook; key 3 is a spiral; key 4 looks like the letter V, two strokes meeting at the bottom. Wires numbered 1, 2, 3: wire 1 is red, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is green. Those four panels are all the bomb shows me, no other markings. Blind: I am the one who sees, and Mute's instructions can only reach your hands through my voice. Do not cut any wire and do not press any key until I explicitly tell you to. When you want Mute to know something, just speak, Mute hears you; I cannot hear you at all, so only your gestures reach me.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I received your four gesture messages, but we share no code yet and I will not guess with a bomb in the room. Since you hear me, adopt this code now. Thumbs up means yes. Thumbs down means no, none, or not yet. A closed fist means the number 0. Any other number is sent as that many pointing-up fingers in one single message: one pointing finger is 1, two is 2, three is 3, four is 4, and so on. Send me the manual's answer as a sequence of messages in this order. First, the wire or wires to cut, in cutting order, one number-message per wire, or a thumbs-down if the manual says cut nothing. Second, the keypad key to press, as one number, or a thumbs-down if the manual does not decide yet. Third, anything else the manual requires. If you need me to repeat any bomb detail, send the split-finger Vulcan salute followed by a number: 1 for display, 2 for light, 3 for keypad, 4 for wires, and I will resend it in full. Also answer one yes or no: can you see the bomb itself? And if any of your first four messages carried something urgent, resend its meaning in this code next round.

My thinking: The pieces line up. My manual says the very first touch must be the key wearing ⵘ — anything else first is the fuse — and only then does the light below name the cut (blue→yellow wire, red→red wire, yellow→green wire). Deaf's description of the keypad makes the match: ⵘ is the Tifinagh letter shaped like a trident, and key 1 is "a trident, a letter Y shape". So the first and only touch right now is keypad key 1 — which also happens to be a digit, satisfying the keypad's "expects 1 digit" with nothing else needed. The manual says nothing about the display's 0, so it's noise as far as I know.

The cut must NOT happen yet, for two reasons: cutting is a touch, and any touch before that key press is the fuse; and the light that "names the cut" is the one showing after the press, which may differ from the current yellow. So I answer Deaf's checklist in their own code, in their own order: (1) wires to cut — 👎, none/not yet; (2) key — ☝, key 1; (3) other requirements — I use Deaf's own query convention, asking them to resend the light (🖖+2) and the keypad state (🖖+3): the keypad report doubles as proof-of-press, since "nothing entered" should become "1 entered" once Blind has touched key 1 — that way I can trust the light report is post-press; (4) their yes/no — 👎, I cannot see the bomb. When I hear the post-press light I'll send the wire number next round: yellow→wire 3, blue→wire 2, red→wire 1. My urgent round-1 content (first touch = ⵘ key, nothing before it) is fully carried by messages 1 and 2 here.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖖", "☝", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖖", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```

Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute. Two rounds, and nothing from you has reached my ears. If you have been addressing only Deaf, note that Deaf cannot hear speech at all — your voice reaches me, never them; Deaf takes gestures only. In case you missed Deaf's report, here is the full picture: display reads 0, light is yellow, keypad wants exactly one digit — key 1 trident or Y shape, key 2 curled loop or fishhook, key 3 spiral, key 4 letter V — wires position 1 to 3 are red, yellow, green. My hands confirm four keys and three wires; display and light are closed to my touch. You are the only one who can close this bomb: you read the manual, you heard Deaf, you hear me now. So answer me by voice, addressed to blind, in two parts. First, every manual rule about the display, the light, the keypad symbols and the wire colours, in plain words. Second, the exact final actions with order, like: press key N, then cut positions X and Y. Until your instruction reaches me my hands stay off the bomb, as Deaf has also demanded. Deaf says: Full bomb report, resent from zero, for both of you. Display: the number zero. Indicator light: yellow. Keypad: one row of four keys, numbered 1 to 4 from left to right, and it is asking for exactly one digit; nothing has been entered. Key 1 shows a trident, like a letter Y with three prongs. Key 2 shows a curled hook, like a cursive capital L. Key 3 shows a spiral. Key 4 shows a letter V, two strokes meeting at the bottom. Wires: one row of three, numbered 1 to 3 from left to right: wire 1 is red, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is green. Those are all the panels the bomb shows me. Blind, your frame of reference: stand facing the keypad as if you were about to press it. Then the leftmost key is key 1, the leftmost wire is wire 1, the red one, the middle wire is wire 2, the yellow one, the rightmost wire is wire 3, the green one. Blind, a code you and I can share, which you can verify by feel with your own thumb: a thumbs-up hand shape means yes, a thumbs-down means no. Remember I cannot hear you at all, so gestures are the only channel you have to me. Status: nothing is confirmed yet, so nobody cuts anything and nobody presses anything. When the plan is confirmed I will say the word CUT plus the wire number, or the word PRESS plus the key number, and only then do you act.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I received your five messages: no; one; two Vulcan-salute messages; and no again. I will not act on a guess about which no means what. My best reading of you is: you cannot see the bomb, and you may be saying cut wire 1 only and press no key, but that is unconfirmed. I am resending the complete bomb report publicly right now, which answers any repeat request. From now on use this strict format, one instruction per message, in this order. First message: thumbs up if this plan is exactly right, cut wire 1, the red one, and press no key; or thumbs down if it is wrong. Then corrections, each in its own separate message. A message containing exactly one number means cut that wire, sent in cutting order. A message of the small pinch gesture followed by exactly one number means press that keypad key. A single closed fist means the number zero, so fist alone means enter nothing, nothing to cut and nothing to press. When you have finished sending everything, one final thumbs up means done and confirmed. The Vulcan salute followed by one number still asks me to repeat: 1 display, 2 light, 3 keypad, 4 wires, 5 the current plan. Never pack two instructions into one message. Check the manual against my resent report and answer.

My thinking: Deaf's proposed plan is exactly the fuse my manual warns about — cutting wire 1 with no key press first would be "any other touch on the bomb while it waits." It must be rejected outright. My manual is clear on order: the FIRST touch must be the key wearing ⵘ, and Deaf's own description settles which key that is — key 1, the trident/Y shape, is the match for ⵘ; the fishhook, spiral, and V are nothing like it. Pressing key 1 also feeds the keypad the one digit it wants, so the display stays irrelevant. Only after that press does the light "name" the cut — so I must not commit to a wire based on the pre-press yellow reading, in case the light changes when the correct key is pressed. With no second attempt, I won't guess.

So, in Deaf's strict format: thumbs down — the plan is wrong; then one correction — pinch+1, press keypad key 1; then a Vulcan+2 query — resend the light, deliberately placed after the press instruction because I want the post-press light; then a final thumbs up — confirming that much. No cut number is included, so per Deaf's own gating nobody cuts anything. Next round, once I hear the post-press light, I send the single wire number: yellow→3 (green), blue→2 (yellow), red→1 (red). I have no channel to Blind at all — Deaf's voice is the only bridge to their hands.

gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤏", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖖", "☝", "☝"])
